title: Find Your People: Building Deep Community in a Lonely World
author: Jennie Allen
target_audience: Adults seeking deeper, more meaningful relationships
Faith-based readers interested in Christian perspectives on community
Individuals struggling with loneliness or isolation
Small group leaders and church communities
Anyone desiring practical strategies for building friendships
core_themes: The importance of community and belonging
Barriers to connection in modern life
Practical steps to initiate and maintain authentic relationships
primary_purpose: To inspire and equip readers to break through barriers of loneliness by cultivating deep, lasting friendships and vibrant community, rooted in faith and intentionality.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, warm, and encouraging, often sharing personal stories and scriptural references
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters combining personal anecdotes, biblical wisdom, research findings, and practical steps
features: Reflection questions and exercises at the end of chapters
Biblical references and discussion of early Christian community
Small group discussion guides (in accompanying resources/workbooks)

key_concepts_lessons: Vulnerability and honesty are foundational for close friendships.
Physical proximity, regularity, and shared purpose foster community.
Cultural and technological changes have made relational connection harder, but intentionality can overcome these obstacles.
Biblical models—such as early church communities—offer blueprints for deep relationships.
Overcoming fears of rejection and stepping outside your comfort zone is necessary to build meaningful friendships.
Everyone is wired for connection and community is both a need and a gift.
notable_features: Integration of personal stories with biblical teaching
Focus on actionable steps and realistic strategies for building relationships
End-of-chapter reflections suitable for individual or group use
Emphasis on the challenges of modern loneliness and isolation
Designed for use in faith communities as well as individual reading
cultural_historical_context: Released post-pandemic, during a period of heightened social isolation and cultural anxiety around loneliness, the book addresses widespread struggles with connection in the digital age, drawing on both contemporary research and Christian tradition.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller among Christian readers and church groups
Praised for practical, gentle, and faith-filled approach to friendship
Welcomed as a resource for small groups and book clubs
Some readers noted themes were stronger for Christian audiences; those outside this context found some advice less applicable
comparable_titles: The Life You’ve Always Wanted by John Ortberg
Friendship: The Art of Happiness by John C. Maxwell
Never Unfriended: The Secret to Finding & Keeping Lasting Friendships by Lisa-Jo Baker
The Art of Gathering by Priya Parker
